title: Linen vs velvet curtains: choosing a texture for your room
description: Compare the visual character of linen and velvet, plan a physical sample check and ask the right questions about composition, lining and care.
imageAlt: Close-up of a light woven curtain surface
body: Start with the room rather than a promise attached to a fabric name. Linen and velvet suggest different visual directions, but neither name tells you everything about a particular curtain. The exact composition, construction, lining and hanging system matter. A photograph can help you choose a direction; a documented physical sample is the basis for the final decision.

sections.heading: Compare the surface in the light you actually use
paragraphs: A linen or linen-look weave often has visible yarn variation and a more relaxed surface. Velvet has a pile that can appear different as you move around it. Neither effect is captured completely by a small screen image. Compare samples vertically near the intended window, then look again under your evening lighting.

Keep the room's other finishes in view. A softly textured neutral might relate to timber and pale paint, while a more directional pile might create a deliberate contrast. This is a styling choice, not a rule that assigns one material to every kind of room.

sections.heading: Read composition before choosing by material name
paragraphs: A fabric described as linen-look may contain no linen. A velvet construction can use different fibres or blends. Ask for the exact composition, usable width and confirmed care label. Where those details are not available, treat the image as an illustrative reference rather than a verified technical specification.
Inspect a larger sample or hanging length where possible. Texture, seams and folds can change the balance of colour compared with a flat swatch, especially when the window is strongly backlit.

sections.heading: Separate appearance from privacy and light control
paragraphs: Do not assume a thick-looking velvet is tested blackout fabric, or that every linen weave will provide the same daylight filtering. Evaluate the actual cloth with any proposed lining. Gaps at the sides and top, the track arrangement and room lighting also affect the result.

If daytime softness and evening coverage are both important, compare a sheer and main layer together. The main fabric can be chosen for its appearance while the complete treatment is assessed against your coverage needs. Confirm the performance of the whole arrangement rather than relying on a generic material label.

sections.heading: Plan the heading, hardware and maintenance
paragraphs: Ask whether the chosen cloth works with your intended heading and existing track or rod. Fullness, stacking room and the fabric's physical behaviour affect the finished arrangement. Use the real fabric width and any pattern repeat when estimating quantities.

Follow the supplier's specific cleaning instructions. Do not assume all linen blends are washable or that all velvets use the same cleaning method. If sunlight exposure or another room condition is a concern, ask about that exact fabric instead of applying an unsupported durability claim.

sections.heading: Make a short comparison before enquiring
paragraphs: Record two or three preferred samples, the room's wall and floor colours, the hanging system and your priorities for light and privacy. Try the available Studio references to explore a palette, then return to physical samples for the final shade decision.

Send your selected fabric references and preliminary measurements with the enquiry. Dcorhome's online references are not a checkout or a promise of stock. Ask the team to confirm the material, sample availability and technical details before committing to a curtain plan.

title: How to layer sheer and main curtains
description: Plan a sheer and main curtain pairing around daylight, evening privacy, independent layers, track clearance and physical sample comparisons.
imageAlt: Daylight passing through softly folded sheer curtains
body: A layered window treatment gives the lighter curtain and the main curtain different jobs. A sheer can soften the appearance of daylight, while a separate main layer can provide additional coverage when needed. The useful question is not simply whether the colours match: it is how the two layers work in the room through the day and evening.

sections.heading: Define the purpose of each layer
paragraphs: List what matters at the window: glare, the view, visual softness, evening privacy or a darker sleeping environment. Do not treat these as interchangeable. An open sheer does not guarantee privacy when the interior is brightly lit, and a dense-looking main fabric is not automatically a tested blackout construction.

Look at the actual window from relevant sightlines and compare samples in daylight and after dark. If stronger light control is required, ask about the exact main fabric, lining and hanging arrangement. The treatment's gaps and coverage matter as well as its cloth.

sections.heading: Check that the hanging system supports two layers
paragraphs: Two independently moving layers need suitable hardware and enough space. Before estimating fabric, record the existing track or rod arrangement, the intended hanging points and any obstructions such as handles, furniture or a deep sill.

Ask the hardware supplier or a competent fitter to confirm capacity, clearances and stacking space. Avoid applying a universal spacing measurement: the correct arrangement depends on the chosen system, headings and the actual fabrics.

sections.heading: Compare undertones rather than matching names
paragraphs: Two fabrics both called ivory can look quite different together. Compare the sheer and main sample beside the room's paint, flooring and upholstery. A close tonal relationship can feel quiet; a stronger contrast can make the window more noticeable.

Hang samples in the intended order where possible. Light passing through the lighter layer can change the apparent colour of nearby surfaces. A large sample is more informative than judging two tiny chips under unrelated shop lighting.

sections.heading: Measure each layer as its own curtain
paragraphs: The sheer and main curtain may have different hanging points, headings, fullness and intended finished edges. Record those assumptions separately. Use the actual usable fabric widths and any verified pattern repeats when planning quantities.

Our measurement tool gives a preliminary estimate, not a cutting instruction. Confirm the final dimensions and allowances with the person responsible for making the curtains. Do not assume that copying the main curtain's figures will produce a correct sheer layer.

sections.heading: Use a preview for direction, then confirm the cloth
paragraphs: Dcorhome's manual Studio lets you explore supported main and sheer selections independently. Its sample-room preview can help you compare a palette. Some room references are view-only; a screen does not establish exact drape, fit, fabric content or light performance.

Save the design on your device or download a supported preview, then include the fabric references and questions in your enquiry. Confirm physical shades, hardware suitability and individual care instructions before deciding. A successful preview is a design aid rather than a stock or performance guarantee.

title: How to choose curtain colours for your bedroom
description: Build a bedroom curtain palette from wall undertones, bedding and lighting, with practical sample checks and separate decisions about privacy and light control.
imageAlt: Full-length curtain folds framing a softly lit interior
body: Choosing a bedroom curtain colour is easier when you compare it with the room you already have. Wall paint, flooring, bedding and the size of the visible curtain area all influence the result. Begin with a small set of directions, then test them in the actual light rather than choosing from a shade name alone.

sections.heading: Start with the largest surfaces
paragraphs: Look first at the walls and floor, then at the bed and other large furniture. Identify whether their colours lean warm, cool or relatively neutral. A curtain does not need to match every object, but it should have a clear relationship to the elements that dominate the room.

If your bedding changes frequently, consider how the curtain will relate to several combinations. A quieter colour can leave room for other accents; a deeper shade can deliberately frame the window. Neither choice is universally better for a bedroom.

sections.heading: See the sample vertically at different times
paragraphs: A fabric on a horizontal table receives light differently from a hanging curtain. Hold a generous sample vertically near the window and compare it again under the lamps used in the evening. Check it beside the wall rather than against an unrelated white screen.

Fold the sample loosely to see highlights and shadows. A textured weave or directional pile may appear lighter or darker across its folds. Screens, photographs and digital recolouring are helpful starting points, but they cannot guarantee the final physical shade.

sections.heading: Decide how prominent the window should feel
paragraphs: A similar tone to the wall can create a quieter transition, while contrast can make the window a focal point. Consider the curtain's full closed area as well as the smaller stack visible during the day. A colour that works in a tiny swatch may feel more prominent across the whole window.

If the room already has a strong wallpaper or patterned bedding, compare a simpler fabric surface before adding another large motif. If you prefer pattern, view enough of its repeat to judge scale and ask how pattern matching affects the estimate.

sections.heading: Keep colour separate from sleep and privacy requirements
paragraphs: A dark colour does not by itself establish blackout performance. A pale colour does not tell you exactly how much privacy a particular fabric provides. Ask about the documented construction, lining and finished coverage when you need stronger light control.

For a two-layer arrangement, compare the sheer with the main fabric in the room. Assess evening sightlines as well as daylight. Confirm track clearances and each layer's hanging point before estimating lengths.

sections.heading: Prepare a useful enquiry
paragraphs: Keep two or three options and note the wall colour, window dimensions, existing hardware and your main concerns. Include the actual reference or shade code where available. A clearly described shortlist is more useful than a long list of unrelated colours.

Explore a supported palette in the Studio and save it on this device, then verify it with physical samples. Ask Dcorhome to confirm composition, available shades and care information for the real fabric. The current demonstration references do not promise purchase availability, installation or a specific finished result.
